episodeTitle.en: How to build a powerful marketing machine | Emily Kramer (Asana, Carta, MKT1)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何打造强大的营销机器 | Emily Kramer（Asana、Carta、MKT1）

guestBioOfficial.en: Emily Kramer led and built the marketing teams at Asana, Carta, Ticketfly, and Astro (acquired by Slack). These days, she’s the co-founder of MKT1, where she helps founders and marketers build and scale their marketing functions. Emily is also a well-respected angel investor and writes my favorite marketing newsletter (MKT1). In today’s episode, she shares her insights on when to hire marketers, how to determine which type of marketing hire is best for your team, how to best work with marketing, and what red flags to look for. Emily shares actionable templates and some incredible frameworks that are sure to expand your marketing knowledge.
guestBioOfficial.zh: Emily Kramer曾在Asana、Carta、Ticketfly和Astro（被Slack收购）领导并建立营销团队。如今，她是MKT1的联合创始人，帮助创始人和营销人员建立并扩展他们的营销职能。Emily还是一位备受尊敬的天使投资人，还撰写了我最喜欢的营销通讯（MKT1）。在今天的节目中，她分享了她对何时聘请营销人员、如何确定哪种类型的营销招聘最适合你的团队、如何最好地与营销部门合作以及应注意哪些危险信号的见解。Emily分享了可行的模板和一些令人惊叹的框架，这些框架必将拓展你的营销知识。

title.en: How to build a powerful marketing machine | Emily Kramer (Asana, Carta, MKT1)
title.zh: 如何打造强大的营销机器 | Emily Kramer（Asana、Carta、MKT1）

summary.en: Emily introduces a "fuel vs. engine" framework for marketing: fuel is the content and value you create, while the engine is how you distribute it to the right people, and the first step before hiring is diagnosing which side is your biggest constraint. For your first marketing hire she recommends a "pie-shaped" (π) generalist who is an expert in one of product, content, or growth marketing, proficient in a second, and able to set strategy across all three. In product-led growth, marketing—not just product—should own top-of-funnel and web conversion, with clear DRIs and a smooth marketing-to-product handoff so the user experience stays consistent. She stresses judging a marketing team by impact goals and full-funnel conversion rates rather than activity metrics, and using lightweight frameworks like AOR (areas of responsibility) lists and GACCS briefs to align marketing and product. Finally, she shares how functional experts can become sought-after angel investors by articulating one clear, specific value-add—such as helping founders build their marketing function.
summary.zh: Emily 提出了一个营销的"燃料 vs 引擎"框架：燃料是你创造的内容和价­值，引擎是你如何把这些送到对的人手里，而在招人之前的第一步，是诊断哪一侧是你最大的瓶颈。关于第一个营销招聘，她推荐招一个"π 型"通才——在产品、内容、增长三类营销中有一项是专家、第二项是熟手，并且能在三者之上定战略。在产品驱动增长（PLG）里，拥有漏斗顶部和网页转化的应该是营销、而不只是产品，并且要有清晰的 DRI 和顺畅的"营销到产品"衔接，让用户体­验保持一致。她强调要用"影响目标"和全漏斗的转化率、而不是"活动指标"来衡量一个营销团队，并用 AOR（责任领域）清单和 GACCS 简报这类轻量框架来对齐营销和产品。最后，她分享职能专家如何把自己清晰、具体的价值贡献（比如帮创始人搭建营销职能）讲清楚，从而变成人人争抢的天使投资人。
